newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb wounds 75, kills children in Algerian market.
newsitem.headline: Bomb wounds 75, kills children in Algerian market.

text.p: A bomb ripped through an Algerian market crowded with people on Friday, killing at least five, including three children, and wounding 75 shoppers and traders, witnesses and hospital sources said.
Algerian security forces put the toll at three dead and 72 wounded, seven seriously.
It was the second such bomb attack on a busy market ahead of Friday Moslem prayers in three weeks.
Friday's bomb went off at 9.15 a.m. (0815 GMT) in the heart of the market in Kolea, a hill town some 30 km (20 miles) southwest of the capital, Algiers.
"The bomb was hidden in a carton, in a pile of others that had been used to bring goods to the market," said one witness.
Four people were killed on the spot, including three children aged about six, witnesses said.
A fifth person died before he could be admitted to hospital, one medical source said.
The source said that of the 75 people taken to nearby Douera hospital, 26 were in a serious condition "and according to the doctors a dozen of these will probably not survive the night."
One witness said community guards, a sort of local police force, had received a phone call on Thursday night saying bombs would explode in Kolea soon.

"Thanks to the rapid intervention of security forces, two other bombs planted in the 'City of 350 Apartments' in Kolea were found and defused," the security forces, quoted by the official news agency APS, said.
It said the toll for the market blast was provisional.

No one claimed responsibility for the bombs but Moslem guerrillas fighting to topple the authorities have been blamed for a series of bomb attacks in which at least 1,400 people have died in the past two years.
The market bomb appeared to be part of a campaign by Moslem guerrillas to dispute assertions that security is improving in the North African country.
Earlier this week, Moslem guerrillas killed at least 34 people in an ambush carried out at a fake security road block.
The security forces gave a death toll of nine for that ambush, but reliable independent newspapers said 34 died, including 20 bus passengers.

"Passengers of a bus were told to get out for identity checks which turned into a nightmare. One by one their throats were coldly slit. Some hostages tried to flee. Some were shot by the terrorists and then finished off and mutilated with knives," said Liberte newspapers.
Diplomats based in Algeria say officials routinely give lower death tolls than reality to echo President Liamine Zeroual's statements that security is improving.

Lack of official action against newspapers -- which operate under tight censorship -- for reporting a higher figure than the official one has long been seen in Algeria as confirmation of the higher toll.
Two Fridays ago a car bomb killed at least seven people and wounded 20 near the market in the town of Boufarik, some 20 km (12 miles) south of Algiers, the security forces reported.

That attack was also carried out just ahead of Friday prayers when markets are crowded with shoppers. The previous weekend, two bombs exploded in two Algerian towns, killing three people and wounding at least 16.

Algerian security forces and Moslem guerrillas have been locked in conflict since the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Islamists had taken a commanding lead. About 50,000 people have since been killed.
Zeroual has promised general elections early next year.
